# Estimates of temporary employment

In this exercise, you can recreate ONS labour market analysis reported in the table [EMP07 Temporary Employees](https://www.ons.gov.uk/employmentandlabourmarket/peopleinwork/employmentandemployeetypes/datasets/temporaryemployeesemp07). This table is updated four times a year in February, May, August and November using the Quarterly Labour Force Survey (QLFS).

Learning outcomes:

-   Add learning outcomes here.

## Data

The data used relates to an estimate for Oct-December 2020.

To follow the exercise, you need to access the relevant dataset from the UK Data Service: [Quarterly Labour Force Survey, October - December, 2020](http://doi.org/10.5255/UKDA-SN-8777-3)

## Get set-up

One you have the data....

```{r}
library(haven)

```

```         
#Open data and keep relevant variables.
lfs_od20 <- haven::read_sav("data/UKDA-8777-spss/spss/spss28
```

Inspect the data.

```         
mydata1 \<- lfs_od20 %\>%select(PERSNO, PWT20, JBTP101, FTPT, INECAC05, JOBTYP, SEX) head(mydata1). 
```

Apply the weight and examine the variable frequencies again.

frq(mydata1$JBTP101, weights = mydata1$PWT20) frq(mydata1$FTPT, weights = mydata1$PWT20) frq(mydata1$INECAC05, weights = mydata1$PWT20) frq(mydata1$JOBTYP, weights = mydata1$PWT20) frq(mydata1$SEX, weights = mydata1$PWT20)

> REVIEW QUESTIONS
>
> 1.  Do the frequencies change noticeably when the weight is applied?
>
> 2.  Run this code to adjust the category order and labels.

::: panel-tabset
## R

```         
mydata1$JobTmp <- rec(mydata1$JBTP101,rec="1=3;2=4;3=1;4=2;5=5;-8,-9=6")

mydata1$JobTmp <-sjlabelled::set_labels(mydata1$JobTmp, labels = c( "Seasonal work", "Done under contract for a fixed period","Agency Temping", "Casual type of work", "Some other reason"))
```

### REVIEW QUESTIONS

When making the table below, which cases are selected in the filter?

head(mydata1$JOBTYP)
head(mydata1$INECAC05)

Create the table.

#\[the labels are missed doe JobTmp, crossreference with above\] #for all mydata1 %\>% filter(JOBTYP==2 & INECAC05==1) %\>% uncount(weights = .\$PWT20) %\>%\
tab(JobTmp, PartTime)

#split by sex and part-time

mydata1 %\>% filter(JOBTYP==2 & INECAC05==1 & SEX==1) %\>% uncount(weights = .\$PWT20) %\>%\
tab(PartTime, JobTmp)

mydata1 %\>% filter(JOBTYP==2 & INECAC05==1 & SEX==2) %\>% uncount(weights = .\$PWT20) %\>%\
tab(PartTime, JobTmp)

> REVIEW QUESTIONS
>
> 1.  How many people are temporary employees (all and part-time) in this quarter?
>
> 2.  How many females are in part-time temporary employment?

Note: You can check if your results match those in the [ONS EMP07 dataset](https://www.ons.gov.uk/employmentandlabourmarket/peopleinwork/employmentandemployeetypes/datasets/temporaryemployeesemp07).

Finally, get unweighted frequencies.

::: panel-tabset
## R

```         
mydata1 %>% filter(JOBTYP==2 & INECAC05==1) %>%tab(JobTmp, PartTime)
```
